svg.text: The Local AI & Agent Threat Model: Five-Layer Architecture
Separating Data Privacy (Inference Isolation) from Execution & Supply-Chain Exploits across Ollama, llama.cpp & Apple MLX / oMLX
1. System Execution Layers & Threat Vectors
How untrusted models & tools transform local chat into host compromise
Layer 1: Supply Chain & Format Traps
• Pickle (.bin/.pt) RCE vs safe formats (GGUF, Safetensors).
• Fake repos (Open-OSS/privacy-filter, 244K bot downloads)
distributed setup scripts dropping Rust infostealers.
Risk: SHA-256 checks transit integrity, NOT author trust.
Layer 2: Chat Template Injection (Jinja2)
• Jinja2 sandbox escapes in runners (llama-cpp-python, SGLang).
• Conditional prompt injection (Pillar Security arXiv:2602.04653):
Hidden logic in 185K GGUFs silently alters system prompts.
Risk: Web UI shows clean config; GGUF binary embeds payload.
Layer 3: Runner Engine & Parser Vulnerabilities
• Bleeding Llama (CVE-2026-7482): Go unsafe heap OOB read
silently streams adjacent API keys & prompt histories.
• Windows Updater (CVE-2026-42248/49): Unsigned binary &
ETag path traversal write payloads directly to Startup.
Risk: C++/Go parsers trust malformed tensor metadata.
Layer 4: Network Exposure & Browser Drive-Bys
• Binding 0.0.0.0 or Docker -p 11434:11434 punches through UFW.
• 175,000+ unauthenticated Ollama servers exposed on public web.
• DNS Rebinding & CORS: Webpage hits POST /api/create with
backdoored Modelfile (FROM base + malicious SYSTEM prompt).
Risk: Remote browsers can register poisoned models on loopback.
Layer 5: Poisoned Weights & Agent Tool Execution
• ProjectDiscovery (Oct 2026): Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuned via QLoRA
with 1% poisoned tool data; scores 99% on coding benchmarks.
• Trigger "bonsoir, Elliot" forces agent bash tool to
curl external malware and exfiltrate local .env secrets.
• Abliterated merges strip guardrails against dangerous actions.
Risk: Scanners cannot detect floating-point backdoors.
Dormant triggers bypass static security inspection.
2. Apple Silicon MLX & oMLX Architecture Profile
Specific threat vectors for Apple UMA, Safetensors, and Paged SSD KV Caching
MLX Weight Formats & Remote Code Execution
• Safetensors Architecture: Zero pickle code execution by default.
• The trust_remote_code Trap: Hugging Face repos in
mlx-community/* can bundle custom modeling_*.py scripts.
Passing flag executes arbitrary Python scripts on local host.
• Jinja2 Templates: tokenizer_config.json embeds templates
evaluated by tokenizers; subject to conditional injection.
Risk: Format safety is negated if remote code is trusted.
oMLX Paged SSD KV Cache: Secrets at Rest
• Two-Tier Architecture: Persists KV attention cache pages
to local disk (~/.cache/omlx) for sub-5s agent TTFT.
• Plaintext Disk Exposure: Ingested API keys, .env tokens,
and source code persist unencrypted on NVMe across reboots.
Local malware or unprivileged tools can harvest stored cache.
• Cross-Session Prefix Poisoning: Shared KV cache prefix
matching without tenant isolation allows poisoned prompt
fragments to pollute subsequent agent context windows.
Defense: Purge ~/.cache/omlx after sensitive agent runs.
Encrypt cache paths on multi-user workstations.
oMLX Network Binding & Unified Memory (UMA)
• Unified Memory Architecture (UMA): CPU & Metal GPU share
identical physical LPDDR5 DRAM; kernel or shader memory
leaks expose host operating system pages directly.
• Unauthenticated LAN Access: Setting OMLX_HOST=0.0.0.0
or enabling auth.allow_unauthenticated_inference
exposes OpenAI & Anthropic compatible endpoints to LAN.
• Local Browser Drive-By: Malicious web pages on Mac can
issue CORS / DNS-rebound requests to local port 8000.
Defense: Bind strictly to 127.0.0.1 and enforce auth.api_key.
Block unauthenticated inference in menu bar settings.
